blocks.text: Within the MITRE ATT&CK framework, taking action on an incident is the key operational transition from investigation to resolution. After an agentic investigation or triage completes, security analysts and AI agents respond by setting investigation verdicts, updating the status, and configuring automated response actions.
The verdict reflects the final conclusion of an incident's investigation.
To view or set the verdict:

blocks.item: In the Agentic SecOps Platform Admin Portal, click Agentic SOC.
In the left-side navigation, click Incidents.
Click an incident.
The Incident Detail page appears. The verdict is located in the top-left region of the page.
See image.

blocks.text: Analysts and agents can set the following verdicts:

blocks.item: Benign: The incident is confirmed to pose no security risk or was successfully blocked inline by existing controls (e.g., ZIA inline policy block).
False Positive: The incident is determined to be a benign event or authorized activity incorrectly flagged as a security threat.
Inconclusive: The incident is unable to be assigned a definitive conclusion automatically due to insufficient telemetry or data access constraints, requiring human analyst follow-up.
Malicious: The incident is a confirmed security threat requiring active remediation or containment workflows.
Suspicious: The incident is flagged with potential threat indicators requiring specialized human expertise to validate due to domain-specific complexity.
True Positive: The incident is a verified security event where the flagged malicious or unauthorized activity accurately represents a real security risk.

blocks.text: The incident status is used to track updates to the investigation.

blocks.item: In the Agentic SecOps Platform Admin Portal, click Agentic SOC.
In the left-side navigation, click Incidents.
Click an incident.
The Incident Detail page appears. The status is located in the top-right region of the page.
See image.

blocks.text: Analysts and AI agents can set the following statuses:

blocks.item: Discovered: The incident was first identified via a series of alerts before any investigation has begun.
Opened: An analyst has begun actively investigating the incident.
Acknowledged: The incident has been reviewed and confirmed to be a legitimate issue requiring further action.
Not Remediated:
Testing: The activity was performed as part of explicit security testing, such as penetration testing.
False Positive: The incident was investigated and determined not to be a security threat.
Authorized Activity: The activity under investigation was necessary for a valid job function.
Confirmed: The incident is closed and the assigned verdict is confirmed to be correct.
Closed: The incident is closed without passing judgment on the assigned verdict.

blocks.text: Playbooks are typically executed when an incident requires remediation, such as when the verdict is set to Malicious or the status is updated to Ready to Remediate. To simplify this process, the Threat Response Recommendation Agent suggests relevant playbooks in the AI Response Actions section of the incident details view.
To manually trigger a playbook from a recommended response action, perform the following steps:

blocks.item: In the Agentic SecOps Platform Admin Portal, click Agentic SOC.
In the left-side navigation, click Incidents.
Click an incident.
The Incident Detail page appears.
On the Details tab, locate the AI Response Actions section.
See image.
Review the recommended playbook for the target entity or incident, taking note of recommendation labels such as Success, Proposed, or Failed.
Click Select Playbook next to the desired action.
If a playbook execution succeeds partially or fails across listed entities, click View to inspect the specific execution status for each individual entity associated with the recommended action.

blocks.text: To learn more about configuring and evaluating playbook execution results, see Managing Playbooks.
